newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-NORMAN SEEKS TO REGAIN TOP RANKING IN MADRID.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN SEEKS TO REGAIN TOP RANKING IN MADRID.

text.p: Greg Norman's tumble from the world number one spot could act as a spur when he plays his first European Tour event of the year, the Spanish Open starting on Thursday.
Norman was replaced at the top of the rankings this week by last year's British Open champion Tom Lehman after a record 96-week run as number one.
The Australian was edged out by one-tenth of a point but could bounce straight back to the top with a top 10 finish in Madrid.

Although Norman has never taken the world ranking system seriously, he will be keen to excel in a field which includes Seve Ballesteros, Jose Maria Olazabal, who finished 12th in the U.S. Masters, Bernhard Langer, seventh in Augusta, and Costantino Rocca, Europe's best in the year's first major in fifth place.
Norman missed the cut in Augusta and will be eager to show his form was only the last vestiges of rustiness after an extensive winter break, as he guests in Madrid in a deal with Ballesteros.
The Spaniard's company Amen Corner and Norman have worked out a deal which will see Ballesteros reciprocate by guesting in Norman's Holden Classic which is likely to be at the start of next year.
Welshman Ian Woosnam has pulled out of the tournament citing "too tight a schedule".
Tour organisers have announced that the O Blue Canyon course on the Thai island of Phuket will stage next year's Johnnie Walker Classic from January 22-25.
